text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today as oil prices retreated from earlier highs. US crude dropped back to $101.91 per barrel after spiking on reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and infrastructure over the past two days—the stock had surged 4.5% on October 16th when those geopolitical tensions first pushed prices up, but traders are now taking profits as the immediate shock fades and the market reassesses the actual risk to global oil supply.

The stock remains up 10.9% over two weeks, reflecting the broader strength in oil prices driven by Middle East tensions. However, today's pullback shows that without fresh escalation in the Strait of Hormuz or Saudi production, the initial rally is cooling—oil explorers and refiners like ConocoPhillips tend to sell off when crisis premiums unwind, even as prices stay elevated.
